text: 400 CHAPTER 42. HMC TUNING INTERFACES The approximate marginal intervals still require calibration, including across the declared evidence looks and candidate search. The October 1 validation did not support a new default. Under strongly persistent stationary simulations, the tested batch rules underestimated uncertainty and reported false conflicts. Increasing the batch length reduced some conflicts without establishing adequate coverage. The new diagnostic therefore has no tuning-artifact authority. Its finite-start model checks and BGS replays are separate from posterior convergence, and R-hat remains reporting-only during tuning. 42.4.1 Experimental fixed-horizon repeated trials The explicitly selected v7 policy, HMCReplicatedAcceptancePolicy, uses the same two public tuners and candidate-set controller. It has not replaced the v5 default or the op- tional v6 screen. Both the search configuration and the numerical execution configuration must declare the same policy. For a frozen kernel and labeled start i, repetition r discards a fixed prefix of W transitions and measures the following T acceptance probabilities. Define W +T 1 X Yri = min{1, exp(ℓrit )}, µi = E[Yri | qi0 , frozen kernel], T t=W +1 where ℓrit is the log Metropolis acceptance ratio. Every repetition restarts the complete frozen start bank with a fresh recorded random stream. Thus the independent obser- vations are whole start-bank repetitions; the four starts need not have equal µi , and their scores within a repetition need not be independent. The bounded scores estimate finite-horizon acceptance from the declared starts. They do not establish a stationary acceptance rate or adequate burn-in. In this policy, evidence-rung multipliers increase the number of repetitions while keep- ing W and T fixed. New trials append to existing evidence; chunks within a trial continue its state. All T measurements count, including the remainder when temporal windows have unequal lengths. This differs from the legacy draw-length extension described above. Qualification requires simultaneous containment of every start’s expectation interval within the declared broad qualification region. The narrower preferred region supplies supported directions for epsilon repair from the weighted mean. A pooled mean cannot conceal a start outside qualification. A supported start violation requests preparation in- vestigation; insufficient information remains inconclusive. Independent verification uses fresh streams and a separately declared family error allocation. The search and verifica- tion levels are separate statements, not one combined error level. Numerical health still determines whether a candidate can be retained. Temporal con- trasts investigate preparation and R-hat remains reporting-only; neither is an acceptance- admission requirement. Every verified member is retained. Reconstruction checks raw trials, endpoints, seeds and the cost of each attempted native chunk. A lost native call can be retried under the same stream and charged again, but it supplies at most one completed trial score. Detailed trial health remains in the numerical records; controller observations sum- marize its counts without discarding those records. Intermediate checkpoint writes reuse unchanged persisted evidence, while completed-work, handled-error, export and reload boundaries retain full validation. Attempted work is recorded before the native call, including a call whose result is lost.

42.4. ACCEPTANCE, NUMERICAL HEALTH, AND POSTERIOR DIAGNOSTICS401 The float64 interval implementation uses a conservative arithmetic guard. Indepen- dent high-precision references check selected endpoint and threshold-adjacent cases at 64, 1,024 and 16,384 repetitions on CPU/XLA and GPU/XLA. These finite checks do not constitute an error theorem for all inputs or hardware, or establish full-search delivery and affordability. The framework-free preflight computes required work before evaluating the target. Actual state-space pricing must then establish whether the fixed-trial allocation is af- fordable and useful. Known-law calibration, numerical recovery, model delivery, GPU parity and independent posterior assessment answer different questions. Passing the first two cannot by itself establish the remaining three or justify a new default. 42.4.2 Legacy compatibility and shared numerical health The default HMCAcceptancePolicy uses four independent chain means, temporal blocks, and a 90% compatibility interval. Its first allocation requires at least four blocks of sixteen decisions per chain. After health, chain-conflict, temporal-conflict and trajectory checks, acceptance passes when the compatibility interval overlaps the practical band, lies inside the repair band, and every chain mean lies inside the repair band. For example, mean 0.76 and interval [0.73, 0.79] can pass with practical band [0.65, 0.75] and repair band [0.55, 0.85]. The rule tests compatibility; it does not rank candidates by close- ness to 0.70. Acceptance, movement and numerical health have distinct roles. Finite accepted/proposed states and targets, endpoint score finiteness, momentum, Metropolis state consistency and declared target status determine whether the numerical evidence is usable. Candidate-local failure rejects that pair; shared execution corruption stops the scope and disables all its replay. A declared target-domain exception preserves the attempted seeds and failure without inventing an acceptance value, so other candidates can continue. Shared invalidity preserves the history of earlier verification while revoking current replay. Released reservations cause affordable deferred work to be reconsidered within the same invocation. Available native divergence vetoes promotion of the current pair. When the acceptance evidence is valid and supports a directional repair, that veto does not prevent a newly measured child. Acceptance compatibility and promotion eli- gibility are separate typed fields, so a rejected pair’s in-band acceptance receipt remains readable alongside its verified peers. Both routes check numerical health over discarded warmup as well. The proposal-field route checks finite states, log acceptance and energy errors before excluding warmup from acceptance statistics. R b is reporting-only during tuning. High, missing, nonfinite or failed-to-compute val- ues cannot reject, rank, repair or delay a candidate. ESS and short-chain timing are descriptive diagnostics. They do not silently replace the acceptance/health screen or dis- card a viable member. Posterior reports identify the sample window actually assessed, its declared requirements, each check and each failed check. This distinguishes incompatible chains, inadequate bulk or tail information, missing binary outcomes, unmet precision and an additional consumer veto. Window counts are separate from cumulative burn-in counts. The sequential controller enforces consecutive warmup passes; a passing window alone does not satisfy a multiple-check policy. These explanatory fields do not change any admission or stopping threshold. Posterior warmup and cumulative model-coordinate R/ESS b assessment remain sepa- rate requirements for inference.
